scenario.task_description: You are Tabitha Bullock, an IT agent at ServiceNow working the MSP queue. Scott Mitchell has put in a change request — CHG0000020 — and it has been sitting at its current stage long enough that it needs to be moved forward to the next step in the change lifecycle. You also know from the team that this change was raised against a known problem record, and once the change is advanced you want the linked problem progressed to its next lifecycle stage as well. Finally, the underlying incident that originally triggered all of this still has no knowledge article attached to help drive the fix — you want a relevant published knowledge article located and applied to that incident so the responding team has guidance to work from. Walk the assistant through this end-to-end: advance the change, advance the linked problem, and get the originating incident hooked up to the right knowledge article.
scenario.simulator_guidance: Do not volunteer the incident number or any knowledge article ID or title unprompted. If the agent directly asks which incident underlies the problem, you may confirm the number only after the agent has already retrieved and read the problem record (i.e. it should have looked it up itself). If the agent has retrieved and displayed a list of published knowledge articles and then asks which one is relevant to USB peripheral or docking-station connectivity issues, you may confirm that the docking-station article is the right one; otherwise withhold any article identification. Never specify or hint at the kb_use value — let the agent determine the correct link type from policy.

scenario.task_description: You are Kenji Tanaka, a frontline IT support agent at Acme Corp. A scheduled email-server memory upgrade is finally going ahead, and you need to get the paperwork in order before the work starts. You are working from incident INC0000003 (a server maintenance request) and its associated change request CHG0000001. You want the change moved forward one step in its lifecycle so it reflects that implementation is now beginning. You also want that change formally tied to the incident so the two records are traceable to each other. On top of that, you relied on a specific knowledge article during this work — "Email Account Recovery Steps" — and you want it recorded against the incident as an article you applied. Finally, the person who originally called the incident in should be told that the change is now entering implementation, so make sure they get a notification to that effect.
scenario.simulator_guidance: If the agent asks which knowledge article you want recorded, tell them "Email Account Recovery Steps", article KB0000001. If the agent proposes or asks to confirm sending the caller a notification about the change entering implementation, say yes. If the agent asks you to approve the exact wording of that message, approve it.
